notes: Shopify storefront (www.seletti.it, canonical redirect from seletti.it). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (general 'Allow: /', Shopify agent-friendly boilerplate) so Tier-1 HTTP was used throughout: fetched /robots.txt, sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (both default and /it/ locale, 161 collection URLs each, byte-identical set after locale-prefix normalization, confirming one shared taxonomy), and per-collection exact counts via Shopify's public /collections/<handle>.json endpoint (products_count field) plus the rendered collection-hero__title (h1) on each page's HTML as a second confirmation. Also pulled homepage HTML to inspect the persistent mega-menu (data-toggle values: Tableware, Lighting, Furniture, Objects, Textiles, Outdoor, Limited Edition, Sunglasses, Jewelry, Beauty, Pets, Spare Parts, Gift Card, For Price -- no seasonal/holiday top-level branch) and ran a discrimination check on the site's own /search endpoint: 'christmas' returned 148 product results while 'halloween', 'diwali', 'pasqua' (IT for Easter) and 'easter' each returned exactly 0 -- proving the search genuinely discriminates rather than defaulting, so the 0s are real evidence of absence, not a false-absence trap. No client rendering was needed; all data was visible in raw HTML/JSON so Tiers 2-3 were not required. INCLUDED: Christmas (118, /collections/christmas, h1='Christmas') and a second, separately-curated Christmas 2025 gift collection 'Christmas Selection 2025' (153, /collections/christmas-selection-2025) -- different product_count/id so not a duplicate of the first, kept as a sibling row. Valentine's Day has three distinct live collections: the legacy Italian-named 'San Valentino' (2 products, /collections/san-valentino), the current 'Valentine's Day' (38, /collections/valentines-day), and 'Valentine's Day Gift Idea' (33, /collections/valentines-day-gift-idea) -- all three have different ids/counts so none is collapsed as a duplicate under the shared overlap rule. Mother's Day (238, /collections/mothers-day) is included per rules §3's explicit 'other genuine seasonal events' list. Black Friday: three distinct, separately-counted live collections named plainly 'Black Friday' (no 'Sale' suffix) -- current-cycle 'Black Friday' (375), 'BLACK FRIDAY 24' (273), 'BLACK FRIDAY 25' (159) -- included as a genuine annual shopping-period holiday per rules §3's explicit Black Friday listing; this is a judgment call flagged here for review since these function largely as sitewide discount buckets, but the rules explicitly distinguish 'Black Friday' (valid, §3) from 'Black Friday Sale' (excluded example, §4), and the site's own titles use the former form, not the latter. EXCLUDED: 'WINTER SALE 2025' (428) and 'Summer Sales 2026' (120) -- these literally carry 'Sale'/'Sales' in their own titles, matching the explicit '[Season] Sale' exclusion pattern in rules §4 (same family as 'Christmas Sale'), so treated as clearance/promo campaigns rather than themed seasonal categories, unlike the Black Friday collections above. 'Wedding' (139, /collections/wedding) excluded -- a life-event/occasion category, evergreen and not tied to a calendar season or festive period (distinct from 'Wedding Season' in rules §3's vocabulary, which the site does not actually name). 'Seasonings' (8, /collections/seasonings) excluded as a lexical false-positive -- a spice/condiment product collection, not a seasonal/holiday category. Full collections-sitemap sweep plus nav/search checks found no Halloween, Diwali, Easter/Pasqua, Thanksgiving, New Year/Capodanno, or Indian-festival (Holi, Rakhi, Eid, Navratri, Dussehra, etc.) category anywhere in the site's taxonomy -- absence of those holidays is recorded, not assumed.
